doc.title: Red Holloway interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995

title: Touring Australia and playing with John Mayall without rehearsals
summary: His 1973 Australian trip with Mayall; Mayall never rehearsed, wanting spontaneity, and paid better than any big band.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Did you say you were going to Australia soon?
Yeah, I’m going the 19th of April.
Yeah, well my first trip to Australia was in 1973 with John Mayall. And in fact Blue Mitchell and Freddy Robinson, I don’t know if you’re familiar with these names—
I remember, did you make a record with him that had no drummer on it or something? I remember hearing a record of his, but I remember your name on it.

Uh, I don’t remember making one with no drummer, but we did do some peculiar things. I remember many times when I first joined him, I said, “Well when we gonna rehearse?” “Oh I don’t have rehearsals.” I said, “What? You don’t have no rehearsals?” I said, “What am I going to play?” “Oh you’ll find something.” I asked Blue Mitchell, I say, “Man, what am I gonna play?” “Oh don’t worry about it, you’ll find something.” He says the reason he doesn’t rehearse is because he likes for it to be spontaneous. Your ideas, he say, he don’t want you to rehearse your ideas to put on the song. He wants you to be able to when you hear it play it. That’s the way he likes it. I said, “Fine with me.” So I just played whatever I felt I wanted to play. “Perfect, perfect!” I said, “That wasn’t shit.” But you know like I noticed that the audience, they went wild. I said, “I can’t believe this, man. What is this?” But it worked, so I said who am I to tell another person how to make his omelet? So, but I must say I enjoyed working with him. I made more money with John Mayall than any big band I ever worked with. And like when we would finish a 15- week tour, in Europe or wherever, he’d say, “Well fellas,” like if we were in Europe, he’d say, “Well I’m going to Spain for two weeks, anybody want to go? Come on, everything is free. You want your ladies sent for, I’ll pay for it.” And he’d maybe give you a couple of grand or a bonus at the end of the tour, stuff like that. I mean of course John Mayall was a millionaire, and he was making 50 or 60 thousand a night. So he could afford to do that, you know? And he like he couldn’t tell you a note big as this room, but he know chords and he could write out the chords to his song but they would be just basic chords, wouldn’t be no flat this and raise that.
